Quick take from Product: we can support a contractual "no customer content for model training" guarantee, but there are two nuance points to clarify in the clause:

1) Definition of "customer content": is it broad enough to include metadata and ephemeral KV cache entries? We should explicitly exclude operational telemetry (CPU/mem/latency, error rates) from "customer content."

2) Runtime signals vs. training data: we can provide aggregated telemetry (counts, anonymized histograms, failure traces) that don't include prompt text. However, for any use that requires access to raw prompts or outputs (for model improvement or labeling), we need explicit opt-in and a secured flow. Building an opt-in ingestion path + UI + audit trail is non-trivial. Rough estimates: 4–6 weeks to add a "training opt-in" pipeline that fans out to a secure S3 bucket with encryption + eventing, plus product work to add the contract gating. If LexCorp only needs aggregated metrics, we can do that immediately (1–2 weeks) via our metrics export.

Impact notes: Dedicated and Private customers may need separate config knobs (we can't assume same telemetry routing for on-prem). Also need to confirm whether they expect subprocessors to see aggregated metrics (analytics vendor) — if yes, that must be surfaced.

Recommendation: propose a compromise clause: (a) Redwood will not use customer content or PII for training; (b) Redwood may use aggregated anonymized telemetry for product improvement; (c) any request to access raw prompts for labeling/training requires customer opt-in and a signed amendment. Priya/Olga — if Legal/Security can sign off on that language, I'll prepare the product-side implementation plan.

-karthik

Security perspective — high level controls we require before signing to any variant that permits telemetry use for model improvement:

- Explicit definition in contract: "customer content" must include prompts, completions, attachments and any user-provided text. Operational telemetry (latency, error codes, aggregated counters) should be explicitly excluded.
- Subprocessor disclosure: LexCorp must accept a (redacted) subprocessors list or a standing process where we provide a signed NDA and then provide full subprocessor details to their security team.
- Technical controls: telemetry must be aggregated and purged after retention window; any raw prompt capture must be opt-in with immutable audit logs and access controls (KMS-wrapped buckets, role-based access, quarterly access review).
- Evidence: SOC2 snapshot or attestation for the telemetry pipeline, plus sample logs showing masking/anonymization.

If LexCorp accepts the three-line compromise Karthik suggested, Security can provisionally sign off assuming we (1) add the opt-in implementation path and (2) include the subprocessor/attestation requirements in the contract. If LexCorp refuses subprocessor disclosure, escalation to Legal/VPs will be needed.

-Olga
Head of Security Engineering

Michael — thank you for the clear proposal and the redlines. We've discussed internally (Product + Security + Legal) and propose the following alternative wording and next steps. Attached is a one-page summary for your legal team (lexcorp_training_clause_proposal.docx). Key points: 

1) Contract language (suggested): "Redwood shall not use Customer Content (defined as user-provided prompts, outputs, attachments, and any personally identifiable information) to train or improve models unless Customer provides explicit, documented opt-in. Redwood may collect and use aggregated, anonymized operational telemetry (e.g., latency, error rates, aggregated prompt lengths) for service improvement and platform health. Such telemetry shall not contain raw prompt or output text."

2) Subprocessors and evidence: we will provide LexCorp's security team with a redacted subprocessor list and a standing process to share full subprocessor details under an NDA. We can also provide a SOC2 snapshot and sample telemetry masking notes.

3) Implementation & timeline: If LexCorp is satisfied with aggregated telemetry only, we can finalize contract edits within 3 business days and enable metrics exports (1 week). If LexCorp requires an opt-in for raw prompt capture for labeling, Product estimates 4–6 weeks to deliver the opt-in pipeline and security controls.

Next steps: please confirm which option LexCorp prefers (aggregated telemetry only, or aggregated + opt-in path). Once confirmed, Priya will draft the contract amendment and Olga will arrange evidence sharing. I'll attach the one-page summary and DocuSign link for the amendment when we have agreement.

Best,
